photos.title: File:Times Square shuttle tracks vc.jpg
photos.description:
Again, just me shaking things up. This is the view you get when you cross over the makeshift platform bridge at Times Square, which crosses over the tracks of the Grand Central Shuttle that connect to the 1, 2 & 3. I had to get a shot of this for my own gratification, lol. I love the infastructure and construction of the subway more than the operational factor so...there you go, lol.

Just a little explanation to give you a better idea of the complexity around here lol. The track to the extreme right is the Grand Central Shuttle track that connects with the uptown local track of the 7th Ave Line. the next one over is the uptown express track, followed by the downtown express and local track in the far distance. The bunch of columns that are moving towards the uptown local track date back to when the subway took a turn east across 42nd Street to Grand Central. So the 7th Avenue Line (south of this point here) was built later.

photos.title: File:Salem United Methodist Church 211 West 129th Street.jpg
photos.description: The Salem United Methodist Church at 211 West 129th Street on the corner of Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard in the Harlem neighborhood of Manhattan, New York City was originally built as the Calvary Methodist Episcopal Church in 1887, and was designed by John Rochester Thomas in the Romanesque Revival style.  It was enlarged in 1890.  The church had the largest auditorium of any Protestant church in the city before the building of Riverside Church.  The Salem United Methodist congregation was founded in 1902 as a mission of St. Mark's United Methodist Church, and became independent in 1908.  It purchased its current home in 1923. having previously worshiped at 102 West 133rd Street.  The renovation of the church in 1949-53 was overseen by Joseph Judge and Samuel Snodgrass. (Sources: From Abyssinian to Zion (2010) and AIA Guide to NYC (5th ed.))

photos.title: File:Glendale Baptist Church 131 West 128th Street.jpg
photos.description: The building which houses the Glendale Baptist Church, at 131 West 128th Street, between Lenox Avenue and Adam Clayton Powell Jr. Boulevard was originally the Manhattan Stables and later became stables for the New York Police Department. The congregation, founded in 1947 as the Zion Baptist Church, worshiped at several locations before New York City sold them the building for $1, moved into the basement of the building in 1954.  The renovation of the building took place over decades. (Sources: Abyssinnian to Zion (2010) and church history)

photos.title: File:South Williamsburg ferry terminal, Schaefer Landing, Williamsburg, Brooklyn, New York - 20221123.jpg
photos.description: The South Williamsburg ferry terminal at Schaefer Landing in Williamsburg, Brooklyn as seen on a November 2022 evening. The culmination of an overall revival in New York-area passenger ferry service that began in the 1990s after several decades of moribundity, the first phase of the NYC Ferry service (including the East River line as seen here) was inaugurated in 2017 by the city government in cooperation with the nonprofit New York City Economic Development Corporation, with boats operated by Hornblower Cruises. New York now has the largest passenger fleet in the United States, with 38 vessels, 25 stations, and seven routes.

photos.title: File:Spirit of America - Staten Island Ferry.jpg
photos.credit: Flickr: Staten Island Ferry "Spirit of America"
photos.description:
The Staten Island Ferry, which takes 25 minutes one way to travel between Battery Park in Manhattan and St. George on Staten Island, is probably the greatest bargain in New York City, as it offers some of the best views of the harbor and the world-famous skyline, for free.
Each of the distinctive double-ended ferries carries a name. This particular one, heading for Staten Island, is named Spirit of America. I am heading for Manhattan on the John F. Kennedy.

In the background, there are a few cranes around the Statue of Liberty; due to security upgrades and renovations, the Statue has been closed since October 2011, and will remain closed through summer 2012.
